recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any future adjustment to AuditEvent.entity.securityLabel wording or binding should be evaluated under later security-label binding decisions such as FHIR-32471 rather than by reopening this DSTU1 rename request.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Security request to replace AuditEvent.object.sensitivity with security-tag terminology and Resource meta security-tag semantics, allowing any security tag rather than a sensitivity-only element.
initial_application: Historical commit 8e1a48066d70501f76de61f4511ec19b48da2df2 changed the then-current AuditEvent spreadsheet source from AuditEvent.object.sensitivity to AuditEvent.object.securityLabel, replaced the old AuditEventObjectSensitivity binding with SecurityLabels, and described the field as security labels applied to the object.
additional_context: AuditEvent is active in source/fhir.ini, and fhir.ini maps the old AuditEvent.object path to the current AuditEvent.entity path. Current source defines AuditEvent.entity.securityLabel. Later Published issue FHIR-32471 changed AuditEvent and similar securityLabel elements to example security-label value sets, explaining why the current binding differs from the older full Resource.meta.security binding. FHIR-7709 is a duplicate of the same 2015 request, and community searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source has no AuditEvent.object.sensitivity or AuditEvent.object.confidentiality element to correct, and the current AuditEvent.entity.securityLabel successor preserves the security-label concept after later model and binding changes.

related_jiras.note: Duplicate issue with the same 2015 AuditEvent.object.sensitivity rename request; it was not independently decided.
